PubMed search_articles rejects queries with more than 20 boolean operators (INVALID_QUERY), so a [uid]-restricted screening of neighbour lists was impossible; screening was done with get_article_metadata instead.
PubMed get_article_metadata returned API_ERROR for one padded batch (PMIDs 2426177, 3014224, 3713193, 6492817, 6864302, 7245090); not retried (low-relevance Shuangshoti neuro-oncology hits).
get_full_text_article PMC2492219 (Brocklehurst 1979, PMID 386891) returned an empty full_text field (scanned pages only); excerpt therefore remains the PubMed abstract and access=pubmed_abstract.
No core PMID (paraphysis as principal subject) has a PMCID; pmc_fulltext access was achieved only for the peripheral record 13242590 (PMC2223811).

Queries with "lamina supraneuroporica" and an OR-chain containing "coronarium" were mis-parsed by PubMed (51k hits); invalid and discarded. "lamina supraneuroporica" and "coronarium" (old lungfish term) have no usable PubMed hit.
Author-handle queries for Sorensen, Studnicka, Rodriguez EM (SCO), Vigh and the OR-block returned homonym noise and were not screened.
Colloid-cyst histogenesis query (64 hits) and the Netsky set (14) were not screened by metadata in this sweep.
Many 1950s-1970s records have no abstract in PubMed (access=metadata_only); their relevance is judged from title/MeSH only and flagged in the note.

records.title: Histological reinterpretation of paraphysis cerebri in Ambystoma mexicanum.
records.authors: Rivas-Manzano P, Torres-Ramírez N, Parra-Gámez L, Ortiz-Hernández R
records.excerpt: In conclusion, we suggest that AEP and PEP are homologous to paraphysis cerebri and the dorsal sac, respectively.
records.note: Developmental histology of the paraphysis cerebri in Ambystoma mexicanum; proposes two extraventricular choroid-plexus-like organs (AEP, PEP) homologous to paraphysis and dorsal sac respectively.

records.title: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis in Bufo bufo larvae.
records.authors: Farnesi RM, Tei S, Vagnetti D, Santarella B, Pollacci P
records.excerpt: A study of the ultrastructure and function of the paraphysis in Bufo bufo larvae was carried out. The structure is a tubular-ramified gland made up of numerous tubules with monolayered epithelial walls surrounded by connective tissue and sinusoids. The epithelial cells secrete glycoprotein to contribute to production of the cephalorachidian fluid. The role of the paraphysis in the transport of fluids and electrolytes from the blood to the cephalorachidian fluid in regulation of ionic and osmotic homeostasis is discussed.
records.note: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis in Bufo bufo larvae: tubular-ramified gland, glycoprotein secretion, proposed role in CSF fluid/electrolyte homeostasis.

records.title: Vasculature of the paraphysis cerebri of the frog.
records.authors: Hinton DA, Nelson SR, Gattone VH
records.journal: Journal of submicroscopic cytology and pathology
records.excerpt: The paraphysis cerebri is a glandular structure found in the third ventricle of lower vertebrates. It is well-developed in amphibians and reptiles. The function of the gland is not substantiated, but may play a role in calcium metabolism.
records.note: Vascular casting + TEM of frog paraphysis: sinusoidal portal system fed by third-ventricle choroid plexus, fenestrated endothelium, possible endocrine role in calcium metabolism.

records.title: Colloid cyst of the third cerebral ventricle with an embryological remnant consistent with paraphysis cerebri in an adult human.
records.authors: Nagaraju S, O'Donovan DG, Cross J, Fernandes H
records.excerpt: The histogenesis of colloid cysts of the third ventricle remains unsettled. Initial theories favored a neuroepithelial (paraphysis, ependyma, choroid plexus) origin and some investigators based on morphologic analysis have offered an alternative endodermal source. We report a case of colloid cyst of the third ventricle arising in association with a remnant which we believe corresponds to the paraphysis cerebri in man.
records.note: Case of adult human colloid cyst with an embryological remnant interpreted as paraphysis cerebri in man.

records.title: Spatiotemporal patterns of Pax3, Pax6, and Pax7 expression in the developing brain of a urodele amphibian, Pleurodeles waltl.
records.authors: Joven A, Morona R, González A, Moreno N
records.excerpt: Pax7 cells were also found in the paraphysis, intermediate lobe of the hypophysis, and basal plate of prosomere 3.
records.note: Pax3/6/7 immunohistochemistry in developing Pleurodeles waltl brain; Pax7-positive cells reported in the paraphysis.

records.title: Localization of three types of arginine vasotocin receptors in the brain and pituitary of the newt Cynops pyrrhogaster.
records.authors: Hasunuma I, Toyoda F, Kadono Y, Yamamoto K, Namiki H, Kikuyama S
records.excerpt: In the paraphysis (possibly the main site of cerebrospinal fluid production), only V2-type receptor mRNA signal and immunoreactivity were detected.
records.note: Newt (Cynops) paraphysis expresses only the V2-type arginine vasotocin receptor; paraphysis described as a possible main site of CSF production.

records.title: An enigmatic eye: the histology of the tuatara pineal complex.
records.excerpt: The histological findings of the pineal eye demonstrated a cornea-like structure, rudimentary lens and simple retina. The adjacent paraphysis was a large, multisaccular organ and the pineal sac a very large saccular organ with a poorly differentiated retina.
records.note: Histology of the neonatal tuatara pineal complex: paraphysis is a large multisaccular organ with apparent secretory function.

records.title: Microvascularization of the pineal gland in the freshwater turtle, Pseudemys scripta elegans (Reptilia): a scanning electron microscopic study of vascular corrosion casts.
records.excerpt: Gross supply, microvascular patterns, and drainage routes of the pineal gland and its vascular relations with associated structures (dorsal sac, paraphysis, choroid plexus of the third ventricle) were studied by scanning electron microscopy of microvascular corrosion casts in 10 specimens of the freshwater turtle, Pseudemys scripta elegans.
records.note: Vascular corrosion casts of the turtle pineal and its relations with dorsal sac, paraphysis and third-ventricle choroid plexus.

records.title: MEMRI for visualizing brain activity after auditory stimulation in frogs.
records.authors: Ringler E, Coates M, Cobo-Cuan A, Harris NG, Narins PM
records.excerpt: We found the greatest change in signal intensity within the torus semicircularis (the principal central auditory region), the habenula, and the paraphysis of frogs that had been exposed to conspecific calls compared with noise or silence conditions.
records.note: MEMRI auditory-stimulation study in Rana pipiens that reports signal change in the paraphysis among other nuclei; the paraphysis is not the study focus.

records.title: Ventricular system and choroid plexuses of the human brain during the embryonic period proper.
records.excerpt: The areae membranaceae rostralis and caudalis are visible in the roof of the fourth ventricle at stage 18, and the paraphysis is appearing.
records.note: Staged human embryos (Carnegie 11-23): ventricular system and choroid plexuses; states that the paraphysis is appearing at stage 18.

records.title: Microsurgical Anterior Transcallosal Resection of Colloid Cysts of the Third Ventricle.
records.authors: Cevik OM, Eksi MS, Guduk M, Usseli MI, Erşen-Danyeli A, Dincer A, Ozduman K, Pamir MN
records.journal: Advances and technical standards in neurosurgery
records.excerpt: In pathological study, the clear staining with PAX-7 points to this pathology being a remnant of the paraphysis.
records.note: Anterior transcallosal colloid-cyst series; PAX-7 staining is interpreted by authors as pointing to a paraphysis remnant.

records.title: Colloid cysts of the third ventricle: ultrastructural features are compatible with endodermal derivation.
records.excerpt: The histogenesis of colloid cyst of the third ventricle remains unsettled. Ultrastructural and immunohistochemical analyses have suggested the following possible origins: (a) neuroepithelium, including paraphysis, ependyma, choroid plexus and tela chorioidea; and (b) endoderm, including respiratory and enteric epithelium.
records.note: Ultrastructure of colloid cyst epithelium compatible with respiratory (endodermal) rather than neuroepithelial/paraphyseal origin.

records.authors: Kim DH, Kwag YN, Kim HS, Kim CS, Han SK
records.excerpt: Korean,, andshared similar apothecial structures but differed in ascospore septation, paraphysis morphology, and substrate preference.
records.note: Fungal (Lachnaceae) taxonomy: botanical/mycological paraphysis, off-topic.

records.title: SPOROGENESIS UNDER ULTRAVIOLET RADIATION IN LAMINARIA DIGITATA (PHAEOPHYCEAE) REVEALS PROTECTION OF PHOTOSENSITIVE MEIOSPORES WITHIN SORAL TISSUE: PHYSIOLOGICAL AND ANATOMICAL EVIDENCE.
records.authors: Gruber A, Roleda MY, Bartsch I, Hanelt D, Wiencke C
records.note: Brown-algae (Laminaria) sporogenesis; off-topic.

records.title: The acrophysis: a unifying concept for enchondral bone growth and its disorders. I. Normal growth.
records.note: Orthopaedic/radiological concept of the acrophysis in endochondral bone growth; not the neural paraphysis.

records.title: Ultrastructure and organization of circumventricular organs and endolymphatic tubules in the treefrog, Hyla versicolor.
records.authors: Kemnitz CP, Fox LM, McNulty JA
records.excerpt: The morphology and anatomical relationship of the paraphysis, anterior choroid plexus, and endolymphatic tubules of Hyla versicolor suggest that these structures may act as a functional unit to regulate composition of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Ependymal cells of both the paraphysis and the choroid plexus exhibit ultrastructural features (an extensive microvillar border, large intercellular spaces containing an amorphous material, and apically located mitochondria) which indicate active exchange between the blood and CSF.
records.note: Ultrastructure of paraphysis, anterior choroid plexus and endolymphatic tubules in a treefrog; proposed to act as a functional unit regulating CSF composition.

records.title: An immunohistochemical study of neuroepithelial (colloid) cysts.
records.excerpt: Theories raised to explain the etiology of colloid cysts have included derivation from the embryonic paraphysis, detachments of developing neuroepithelium from the tela choroidea, and remnants of respiratory epithelium; a more recent theory suggests that these cysts are products of developing choroid plexus or ependyma.
records.note: Immunohistochemistry shows colloid-cyst epithelium differs from choroid plexus/ependyma; lists embryonic paraphysis among proposed origins.

records.title: A survey of occurrence of about seventeen circumventricular organs in brains of various vertebrates with special reference to lower groups.
records.excerpt: The paraphysis is found in the dogfish (Mustelus) and the osteoglossomorphous teleosts (Osteoglossum and Gnathonemus). The so-called paraphysis of the lungfish is not a paraphysis, but a dorsal sac.
records.note: Comparative survey of ~17 circumventricular organs in 31 vertebrate species; reports paraphysis in dogfish and osteoglossomorph teleosts and states the lungfish "paraphysis" is a dorsal sac.

records.title: Occurrence of bone fractures and parathyroid hyperplasia in paraphysectomized frogs (Rana catesbeiana).
records.authors: Nelson SR, Foltz FM, Camarata P, Sarras MP
records.excerpt: These findings indicate the paraphysis plays a role in calcium metabolism, possibly by producing a factor necessary for calcium action on cells.
records.note: Paraphysectomy of bullfrog tadpoles leads to parathyroid enlargement and bone fractures 22 months later; supports a role of the paraphysis in calcium metabolism.

records.title: Ultracytochemical localization of Ca++-ATPase activity in the paraphyseal epithelial cells of the frog, Rana esculenta.
records.authors: Ueno S, Umar H, Bambauer HJ, Ueck M
records.excerpt: Ca++-ATPase activity was studied ultracytochemically (cf. Ando et al. 1981) in the paraphysis cerebri of the frog. An intense reaction was demonstrated on the plasmalemma of the microvilli at the apical pole of paraphyseal cells; in contrast, the basolateral plasmalemma showed only a slight staining.
records.note: Ultracytochemistry of Ca++-ATPase in frog paraphysis cerebri; apical microvillar plasmalemma strongly reactive; paraphyseal epithelium proposed as a Ca-ion regulator of CSF.

records.title: Lissencephaly: computed tomographic diagnosis.
records.excerpt: Most of these changes were demonstrated on computed tomography, and include lack of cortical sulci and gyri; calcification in the region of paraphysis; wide, shallow sylvian fissures; colpocephaly; poor development of white matter; and persistent cavum septum pellucidum and cavum vergae.
records.note: CT description of lissencephaly that uses "calcification in the region of paraphysis" in passing; not a study of the paraphysis.

records.title: Hypocalcemia and motor neuron degeneration in paraphysectomized frogs.
records.excerpt: The paraphysis has been studied extensively but its function is unknown. Surgical removal of the paraphysis in the bullfrog (Rana catesbeiana) resulted in hypocalcemia and tetany in 35 frogs, about 40% of those operated upon.
records.note: Surgical removal of the bullfrog paraphysis causes hypocalcemia and tetany in about 40% of frogs, with secondary motor-neuron degeneration.

records.title: [Statistical study of the colloid cyst of the 3rd ventricle (so-called cyst of the paraphysis). Clinico-anatomical series of 75 cases].
records.excerpt: Known as the paraphysis cyst, or the colloid cyst of the third ventricle, the lesion described in this study continues to have an unprecise etiology in spite of a great number of investigations.
records.note: Series of 75 colloid cysts (the "cyst of the paraphysis"); author concludes embryological work does not clarify origin; male predominance.

records.title: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis cerebri of the water snake Natrix maura L.
records.authors: Fernández-Llebrez P, Becerra J, Marín-Girón F
records.excerpt: Paraphyseal epithelial cells of Natrix maura have been studied with light and electron microscopy. They showed a clear polarity apically related to the third ventricle and, basally, to a connective tissue layer which surrounded the whole organ.
records.note: Light and electron microscopy of snake paraphyseal epithelium: polarised cells with microvilli, fenestrated sinusoids, proposed CSF-blood exchange role.

records.title: The significance of the evolution of the cerebrospinal fluid system.
records.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
records.excerpt: The ventricular system, the roof of the hindbrain, the meninges and subarachnoid space, the ependyma with its various derivatives, including the choroid plexuses and paraphysis, and the relationship between the various CSF compartments and the cerebrovascular system have all been compared in these animals.
records.note: Comparative morphology of the CSF system from amphioxus to mouse including choroid plexuses and paraphysis; hypothesis that the CSF system maintains the chemical environment of CNS cells. PMC full text for PMC2492219 returned empty (scanned images only), so the excerpt is the PubMed abstract.

records.title: The pineal-paraphyseal complex of sea turtles. I. Light microscopic description.
records.excerpt: The complex was examined by light microscopy in several age classes of green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) and from juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta). The paraphysis is extensively fused to the distal portion of the pineal body, suggesting an interrelated function for these two tissues.
records.note: Light microscopy of the large pineal-paraphyseal complex of green and loggerhead sea turtles; paraphysis fused to the distal pineal.

records.title: A comparative study of the pineal complex in the deep-sea fishes Bathylagus Wesethi and Nezumia liolepis.
records.excerpt: A dorsal sac and a paraphysis were found in B. wesethi; both structures are absent in N. liolepis.
records.note: Pineal complexes of two deep-sea teleosts: a dorsal sac and a paraphysis present in Bathylagus, absent in Nezumia; functional relation of dorsal sac, paraphysis and pineal lumen suggested.

records.title: Neuroepithelial (colloid) cysts. Pathogenesis and unusual features.
records.authors: Palacios E, Azar-Kia B, Shannon M, Messina AV
records.excerpt: An origin more diffuse than the paraphysis seems most likely in our opinion, and we attempt to substantiate this theory with several of the cases from our series.
records.note: Radiological case series on neuroepithelial cysts; argues for an origin more diffuse than the paraphysis.

records.title: [Pineal organ and parietal eye of Lacerta vivipara: a qualitative and quantitative microscopic study of the uptake of 3H-5-hydroxytryptophan during ontogenesis].
records.authors: Meiniel A, Collin J-P, Roux M
records.excerpt: In contrast, the weak nonspecific reactions, in the neighbouring brain structures (dorsal telencephalon, tectum opticum and paraphysis), stay constant.
records.note: Embryonic lizard epiphysis labelling with 3H-5-HTP; the paraphysis serves only as a neighbouring brain structure with constant weak non-specific reaction.

records.note: Frog subfornical organ proposed to regulate paraphyseal secretory activity; abstract not available in PubMed.

records.title: An electron microscopic study of the choroid plexuses of Necturus maculosus.
records.note: EM of choroid plexuses of the mudpuppy (urodele); background for telencephalic/diencephalic plexus ultrastructure; abstract not available.

records.title: Contribution to the study of the epithalamus of Bufo arenarum (Hensel). I. Histological observations on the epiphysis cerebri.
records.note: Histology of the epiphysis cerebri (and associated choroid plexus per MeSH) in a toad; abstract not available.

records.title: Development of the choroid plexus.
records.authors: Dziegielewska KM, Ek J, Habgood MD, Saunders NR
records.excerpt: Mammalian choroid plexuses develop at four sites in the roof of the neural tube shortly after its closure, in the order IVth, lateral, and IIIrd ventricles.
records.note: Review of choroid plexus development including the site of the third-ventricle plexus in the neural tube roof.

records.title: Intracellular plasma proteins in human fetal choroid plexus during development. I. Developmental stages in relation to the number of epithelial cells which contain albumin in telencephalic, diencephalic and myelencephalic choroid plexus.
records.authors: Jacobsen M, Clausen PP, Jacobsen GK, Saunders NR, Møllgård K
records.excerpt: The developmental stages of telencephalic, diencephalic and myelencephalic choroid plexuses in the human fetus and the morphology of choroid plexus epithelial cells in the various plexuses in different development stages were described on basis of PAS- and toluidine blue-stained material.
records.note: Developmental stages of human fetal telencephalic/diencephalic/myelencephalic choroid plexus; background for the telencephalic plexus that adjoins the paraphysis.

records.title: [Structural organization of choroid plexus primordium in human telencephalon].
records.excerpt: Using the methods of light and electron microscopy and immunocytochemistry, the structure of choroid plexus primordium of telencephalon (epithelial plate) was studied in human embryos at weeks 5-6 of development.
records.note: Light/EM/immunocytochemistry of the telencephalic choroid plexus primordium in 5-6 week human embryos.

records.title: The human brain at stage 17, including the appearance of the future olfactory bulb and the first amygdaloid nuclei.
records.excerpt: The beginning of the future choroid plexus consists in the formation of blood vessels and necrotic changes in the roof of the telencephalon medium and in rostral growth of the anterior choroid artery.
records.note: Carnegie stage 17 human brain; choroid plexus begins in the roof of the telencephalon medium.

records.title: The development of the human brain and the closure of the rostral neuropore at stage 11.
records.excerpt: The brain comprises telencephalon medium (represented by the embryonic lamina terminalis) and a series of neuromeres: 2 for the forebrain (D1 and D2), 1 for the midbrain, and 6-7 for the hindbrain (RhA-C; RhD is not clearly delineated).
records.note: Stage 11 human brain: defines telencephalon medium as the embryonic lamina terminalis (terminology background).

records.title: The initial development of the human brain.
records.excerpt: The early appearance of the telencephalon medium (before cerebral vesicles have formed) is stressed, and the terminological implications for the subdivisions of the brain are discussed.
records.note: Early human brain development; emphasises the early appearance of the telencephalon medium and discusses terminology of brain subdivisions.

records.title: The longitudinal growth of the neuromeres and the resulting brain in the human embryo.
records.excerpt: The most cephalic neuromere is the telencephalon medium, abbreviated T1 here.
records.note: Neuromeric growth in staged human embryos; telencephalon medium designated T1 (terminology background).

records.title: Telencephalon Cytoarchitecture of tsinling dwarf skinks (Scincella tsinlingensis).
records.authors: Yang C, Li L, Kou Z, Zhang H, Wang L, Zhao Y, Zhu N
records.excerpt: The telencephalon of S. tsinlingensis was consisted of paired olfactory bulbs, paired cerebral hemispheres, and a telencephalon medium or impar.
records.note: Lizard telencephalon description using the term "telencephalon medium or impar"; no paraphysis data in the abstract.

records.title: A reinterpretation of the cytoarchitectonics of the telencephalon of the comoran coelacanth.
records.excerpt: In coelacanths, the telencephalon is divided into pedunculated olfactory bulbs, paired hemispheres, and an unevaginated telencephalon impar.
records.note: Coelacanth telencephalon with an unevaginated telencephalon impar (reinterpreted as medial amygdalar nucleus); phylogenetic background for the telencephalon impar.

records.title: Morphogenesis of the rat forebrain.
records.authors: Alicelebić S, Mornjaković Z, Kundurović Z
records.journal: Bosnian journal of basic medical sciences
records.excerpt: E15: the main event is the appearance of the origins of plexus choroideus in the area of telencephalon impar as fingerlike processes.
records.note: Rat forebrain morphogenesis E12-E16; choroid plexus origins appear in the area of the telencephalon impar.

records.title: Telencephalon "impar", "semipar" and "totopar". (Morphogenetic, tectogenetic and architectonic definitions).
records.note: Definition of telencephalon impar/semipar/totopar (terminology); abstract not available.

records.title: Third ventricle suprachoroidal cells.
records.excerpt: Using transmission electron microscopy two types of cells on the choroid plexus of the third ventricle of the frog Rana esculenta have been located. They lie on the microvilli and cilia of the choroid epithelium. Their free surface is in contact with the cerebrospinal fluid.
records.note: EM of cells lying on the third-ventricle choroid plexus of Rana esculenta (suprachoroidal/Kolmer-like cells); neighbour of the frog paraphysis papers.
